text_blocks.snippet: Federal prosecutors and the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois are warning residents about a sharp increase in sophisticated phone, text, and door-to-door scams across the region.

snippet_links.text: Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois

text_blocks.snippet: Active Scam Alerts in Central Illinois

list.snippet: U.S. Attorney's Office Impersonation: Scammers spoof official federal numbers and use real staff names to demand immediate payment or sensitive financial details over the phone . Federal agencies never request money or financial data by phone.

Fake Traffic & Tollway Texts: Fraudulent text messages claim recipients owe unpaid fines for traffic or toll violations. These phishing texts contain malicious links designed to steal personal and financial data.
Storm Chasers & Home Repair Fraud: Unsolicited door-to-door contractors pressure homeowners for upfront cash payments for urgent roof, gutter, chimney, or driveway repairs following severe weather.

Online Shopping & Tariff Traps: Fraudulent social media ads offer steep discounts on popular goods, followed by fake follow-up demands for extra cash to cover shipping "tariffs" before items are released.
Never click links in unsolicited text messages or emails regarding unpaid fines or package deliveries.
Verify directly by looking up official organization contact numbers rather than using numbers provided in suspicious messages.
Check local contractors through resources like the BBB Scam Stop Program before signing agreements or paying upfront .
